summary:
Every rating across the board is lit up the same way right now, which tells you this is a systemic trend, not noise in one model. R1 through R4 are all running identical 14-day lines — 5-1 (83%, n=6) in trends, runs, sp, and hitting, with sp carrying a 3-game win streak on every rating. The flip side is just as uniform: bullpen_fatigue is ice cold across R1-R4, sitting 1-5 (17%, n=6) with a 5-game losing streak on all four ratings. That's as clean a fade signal as you'll see — if today's slate has any plays leaning on bullpen_fatigue as a primary category, treat them skeptically regardless of rating, while plays stacking trends+sp or trends+runs deserve full confidence given both the live heat and the season-long category-combo edges (trends+sp leads all combos at 58.0%, 370-268 n=638; trends+runs close behind at 57.3%).

On today's board, prioritize games where R2 is attached — it's the only rating showing positive 7-day unit flow among strong plays (+1.0u, 2-1) and it's running hottest over 30 days at 9-4 (69%, +5.0u, n=13), clearly outpacing R4's flat 30-day stretch (4-4, +0.0u). If MIL, TBR, BOS, or LAD show up as model favorites today, lean in hard: all four are strong-play machines when liked, with LAD the standout at 80% (28-7, +27.0u) and BOS right behind at 76% (22-7, +19.0u). Conversely, any slate appearance from NYY should get discounted — the model is barely coin-flip on them overall (23-24, 49%) and actively bleeds units on strong NYY plays (9-14, -4.0u). Given the identical hot/cold pattern across all four ratings, today's edge isn't about picking the right rating — it's about picking the right category. Stack trends with sp or runs wherever the slate allows, avoid leaning on bullpen_fatigue as a tiebreaker, and let team trust (MIL, TBR, BOS, LAD) break any close calls between otherwise similar rated games.
